# Mycobacterium avium complex infection

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Pulmonology > Infectious lung diseases > Mycobacterium avium complex infection*

[Original Article Link](/library/xH0Esh)

---

## Summary

<u>Mycobacterium avium complex</u> (<u>MAC</u>) infection is caused by the <u>Mycobacterium avium</u> complex (<u>M. avium</u> and <u>M. intracellulare</u>). It more commonly occurs in patients with advanced <u>immunosuppression</u> and is considered an <u>AIDS-defining condition</u>. Diagnosis is based on isolation of the organism (<u>acid-fast bacilli</u>) on culture and treatment consists of at least two anti-<u>mycobacterial</u> drugs (e.g., a <u>macrolide</u> with <u>ethambutol</u>).

---

## Etiology

* Caused by the <u>Mycobacterium avium</u> complex, which consists of the ubiquitous pathogens <u>M. avium</u> and <u>M. intracellulare</u>.

* <u>AIDS-defining</u> condition; frequent opportunistic bacterial infection in patients with <u>AIDS</u>

* Infection occurs via the gastrointestinal or <u>respiratory epithelium</u> through inhalation, ingestion, or <u>inoculation</u>.

* Bacteria may remain confined to the area of entry (localized) or spread via <u>the lymphatic system</u> and the blood (disseminated).





References: [[2]](/library/05XeiA)

---

## Clinical features

<u>MAC</u> infection often manifests as disseminated disease and typically occurs in patients with advanced <u>immunosuppression</u> (<u>CD4 counts</u> < 50/mmÂ³). [[2]](/library/05XeiA)




* Night sweats, <u>fever</u>, weight loss

* Focal <u>lymphadenitis</u>

* Abdominal pains, <u>diarrhea</u>

* <u>Hepatomegaly</u>, <u>splenomegaly</u>

* <u>Localized symptoms</u> depend on the organ system involved and include <u>pericarditis</u>, <u>cough</u>, <u>joint</u> pains, or signs of <u>CNS</u> infection.

---

## Diagnosis

Diagnosis of disseminated <u>MAC</u> is based on isolation of the organism in a patient with characteristic clinical features.  [[2]](/library/05XeiA)




* <u>Laboratory studies</u>

* <u>CBC</u>: <u>anemia</u>, <u>leukopenia</u>

* <u>CMP</u>: ↑ <u>alkaline phosphatase</u>, ↑ <u>gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase</u>, ↑ <u>LDH</u>, ↓ <u>albumin</u> [[3]](/library/BGXzY-)

* Isolation of the organism (<u>confirmatory test</u>): <u>acid-fast bacilli</u> staining and culture from blood, <u>bone marrow</u>, <u>lymph nodes</u>, or other sterile tissue or body fluids

* Imaging: depends on the presenting symptoms; examples include

* <u>Chest x-ray</u>/CT chest: variable findings including diffuse pulmonary opacities, <u>lymphadenopathy</u>; may appear normal

* CT abdomen: <u>retroperitoneal</u> and <u>mesenteric</u> <u>lymphadenopathy</u>, <u>hepatosplenomegaly</u>, thickening of the <u>small bowel</u> wall





> [!TIP]
> Disseminated <u>MAC</u> may mimic <u>disseminated TB</u>. Findings that favor <u>MAC</u> include elevated <u>alkaline phosphatase</u> and <u>gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase</u>, <u>hepatosplenomegaly</u>, and <u>leukopenia</u>. [[3]](/library/BGXzY-)

---

## Treatment

Manage all patients in consultation with an infectious disease specialist. In patients with <u>HIV</u>, initiate <u>ART</u> (if not already started) concurrently with <u>MAC</u> treatment.




* Initial regimen [[2]](/library/05XeiA)
* At least two-<u>antimycobacterial drugs</u>; preferred agents include:

* <u>Macrolide</u>: <u>clarithromycin</u>;  DOSAGE (first-line) OR <u>azithromycin</u> DOSAGE

* AND <u>ethambutol</u> DOSAGE

* Optional third and fourth drugs [[2]](/library/05XeiA)

* Consider in patients with any of the following:

* A high risk of mortality (e.g., <u>CD4 count</u> < 50/mmÂ³)

* Drug resistance

* High <u>mycobacterial</u> load

* Inadequate response to <u>ART</u>

* Agents (any of the following):

* <u>Rifabutin</u> DOSAGE

* <u>Fluoroquinolone</u>: <u>levofloxacin</u> DOSAGE or <u>moxifloxacin</u> DOSAGE

* Injectable agent: <u>amikacin</u> DOSAGE or <u>streptomycin</u> DOSAGE
